en.title: Earliest Match with a Single-Character Wildcard
en.description:
Find the first occurrence of the pattern in the text, where * stands for exactly one arbitrary character rather than a string of any length. Return −1 if there is none; indices start from 0.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and the solution; supplements for missing source bounds and example corrections are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: Two lines s and p. In the original, the text s is a..z, and the pattern p is a..z with at most one *; the original has no length bound, and this site uses 0≤length of each string≤200000. An empty pattern matches at 0.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 0; -1; 0. Checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Split the pattern at the asterisk into two parts, mark the occurrences of each part with KMP, then check both parts at each starting point; with no asterisk, run KMP only once.
